For example, the chambers of commerce of Dallas, Houston, and Pittsburgh, among others, supported the formula adopted herein. Many shippers also expressed their support. Shippers in certain locales supported the proposal on a broad basis but stated that a specific city was not adequately covered. A prime example of this is Atlanta, but, as previously indicated, there is no practical solution to that particular problem within the confines of a general rule. Similarly, the Puget Sound Traffic Association and the Port of Bremerton request respectively that an area South of Tacoma and certain property owned by the Port be included within the Seattle commercial zone. The stated purpose of this proceeding is to determine on a board basis whether commercial zones should be expanded, and specific consideration of these particular areas is more properly handled through a petition seeking an individual determination. In light of shipper efforts to bring the special problems in applying the formula to certain communities to our attention in this proceeding, petitions for individual determinations filed with respect to the effected municipalities will be handled on an expedited basis. Moreover, we have a simple letter petition procedure for the consideration of possible inclusion of such special problem areas. In the meantime, the Seattle commercial zone will experience a great increase in size through application of the new formula (encompassing Bremerton, Everett, and Tacoma) and the economic health of the specific areas should not be stymied for they will have the traditional means of regulated motor carriage available.
